Maria L: Heads-up — during the 05:00 probe window we saw sustained small-tenant SLO bumps (99p token latency). Not full incident but concerning. @Kevin H can you take a look?
Kevin H: saw it. pattern looks like rapid idle->hot bursts. lease rebalancer hands off too slowly and those tenants momentarily consume shared admission.
Jamal: also saw cache churn (prefix KV misses) which amplifies tokens-to-latency. The two together hit the tail.
Kevin H: thinking out loud: add a lightweight smoothing admission layer between ingress and lease allocator. It applies an exponentially decaying burst score per tenant and throttles recent bursts proportionally. Not a permanent quota, just a dampener to avoid stealing global headroom.
Priya: so effectively a leaky-bucket on top of leases. How do we avoid blocking legitimate ramp-ups (eg overnight batch->interactive transition)?
Kevin H: exactly — not a hard block. Proposal: compute burstScore = sum(tokens * exp(-(now - t)/tau)). admission_factor = 1 - clamp(burstScore / burst_threshold, 0, 1). final_allowed = base_lease * admission_factor. For PLG tiers we can convert to a probabilistic admission (soft fail) instead of strict cap.
Sam: probabilistic admission is friendlier for UX. Would return 202 + Retry-After or stream with degraded rate.
Kevin H: pseudo-code sketch:
```
on_request(req):
  tenant = req.tenant
  now = time()
  // decay existing score
  tenant.score *= exp(-(now - tenant.last_seen)/tau)
  tenant.score += req.tokens
  tenant.last_seen = now
  factor = 1 - min(tenant.score / BURST_THRESH, 1)
  if random() > map_to_prob(factor, tier):
    return soft_reject() 
  else:
    forward_to_lease_allocator(req)
```
This keeps most logic local and cheap, and we only consult the lease layer when soft check passes.
Maria L: telemetry? what do we need to validate effectiveness?
Jamal: emit: burstScore histogram, admission_factor timeseries, soft_reject rate by tenant tier, correlation with prefix-cache-miss rate. Add labels: burst_decay_tau, burst_threshold to experiment metadata.
Priya: config + rollout plan: feature flag default=observer (emit metrics only) -> post-only (count but still forward) -> probabilistic enforcement -> hard enforcement if safe. Also config must be service-scoped and plumbed through infra-config.
ops-bot: deploy queued: canary to infra-staging in 1h (command: /deploy canary smoothing-admission) :rocket:
Kevin H: abuse signals: tie burstScore into abuse-detection. If a tenant shows adversarial token patterns (rapid retries, many short requests) escalate to penalty window (longer decay or temporary probation).
Jamal: also ensure fallback to model-variant routing: if latency rises, prefer cheaper smaller-context variants automatically as part of degrade policy.
Priya: privacy note: only store aggregated burstScore and last_seen per tenant. no request bodies in logs. compliance will need a short blurb in RFC.
Sam: perf tests: need synthetic traffic profiles: legitimate ramp-up, PLG bot-style burst, multi-tenant correlated bursts. Measure tail latency, admission fairness delta, and false-positive soft_reject rate.
Maria L: ok. I'll open an RFC draft in eng-infra/rfcs with goals, math, config knobs, telemetry, migration steps, and perf plan. Ping when draft is up and we'll iterate. :thumbsup:
Kevin H: will add perf harness and pseudo-code + test scripts.
Sam: +1 on eval cases, will add bot patterns.
Priya: I'll coordinate compliance review once RFC lands.
Maria L: thanks everyone — leaving follow-ups in the RFC thread.
